convoLines.text: "People are smiling. I forgot what that looked like."
"There's still the matter of the murder of Henry. Nobody's settled it."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
Another crack. The telling doesn't hold together anymore.
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? I'm practicing what I would say if I ever saw my family again. I haven't told anyone."
Scarlett has an edge today — something curdled.
"There's still the matter of the murder of Henry. Nobody's settled it."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Counted.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Okay so — Still on their secret."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Every laugh out there feels wrong today. Then I feel wrong for thinking it."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
At the trap line the ground is torn up. Something was here, recently, and it wasn't careful. Adrian's hand finds your sleeve. You leave together, faster than you came.
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
Adrian blinks, then groans. "Oh, that's my fault, I worded that terribly. What I meant was..." The real version is boring, which is how you know it's true.
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"That's not — that's not what happened." Adrian's hands won't stop moving. "You're twisting things."
"Finally. I was wondering when you'd see my value."
A long exhale. "I'll get there. Just needed a minute where I didn't have to be fine."
"I've got things to do. People to avoid. You know."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet."
"Heh. Nobody's asked me that in a while. ...I'm alright. Getting there."
"Mehret always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sleep's gone strange. I tend the fire without being asked at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Here's the thing — Still on what's been happening."
You show them Wild Ramps — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I keep expecting to see them by the fire. Then I remember."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
At the ridge the ground is torn up. Something was here, recently, and it wasn't careful. Adrian's hand finds your sleeve. You leave together, faster than you came.
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
*They've deflected you before. The evidence needs to be heavier this time — one more thread before you speak.*

"Fine." Sharp. "You want the truth? I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to be in charge. You looked at me like I mattered, and I wanted to keep that. So I gave you someone worth looking at. That person isn't real. This one is —
and it's worse, isn't it? Happy now?"
"You're kind. Don't let this place change that."
"Oliver always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Finally. I was wondering when you'd see my value."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"My cut needs a second pair of hands. Will you help me clean it?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Oliver owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Hey — I found some Purslane today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Ekrem shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that plant lesson."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Walk the perimeter with me? Quiet company. No big talk."
They nod. "Okay."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. I know the ridge above the creek — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"We were just talking. Nothing important."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? I don't actually know how to swim and I'm terrified someone will find out."
Ekrem has an edge today — something curdled.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on their secret."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Wild Ramps — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Okay, real question: what's the funniest thing you've seen since we got here? I desperately need it."
They laugh — really laugh, the first real one you've heard in days. "Okay. Okay, that's good. I needed that."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"Still on the funniest thing you've seen."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
It's quiet at the tree line. Maya doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"They took Hassan — Lie Detector, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Okay — I need to move. But I'm glad we talked."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"How are you holding up? Honestly. No performance."
"Thank you for saying it straight. Most people perform. I'm tired of performances." You feel oddly steadier.
"This one — Shepherd's Purse. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Finally. I was wondering when you'd see my value."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the ridge above the creek — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
As I said — Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"As I said — We were just talking. Nothing important."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I asked Scarlett about this wound — Scarlett's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
As I said — Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "I dreamed Scarlett was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
